summary: The root خفت (khft) primarily describes a voice becoming still, silent, low, or weak. It extends to mean ceasing to speak, dying, or dying suddenly.
lane: 1 خَفَتَ خاف خف خفى خفت خفتت , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. خَفِتَ , (Msb,) inf. n. خُفُوتٌ (S, A, K) and خَفْتٌ (Msb, TA) and خُفَاتٌ , (TA,) It (the voice, S, A, Msb) was, or became, still, (S, K,) or silent; (A;) was, or became, low, (Msb,) or soft, or gentle, or slender; and became weak, by reason of vehement hunger. (TA.) -b2- Hence, said of a dying man, He ceased speaking; (S;) he was, or became, silent; (S, A, K;) he spoke not. (A.) -b3- And [hence,] خَفَتَ , (A, TA,) inf. n. خُفُوتٌ . (assumed tropical:) He died: (A, TA:) and خَفَتَ , inf. n. خُفَاتٌ , (tropical:) he died suddenly; (AA, S, K, TA;) as also مَاتَ خُفَاتًا . (A.) And the latter, i. e. خَفَتَ inf. n. خُفَاتٌ , accord. to AM, (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, weak, and abject, or abased. (TA.) -b4- خَفْتٌ also signifies The speaking with a suppressed voice; and so , (S, K, TA,) and . (K, TA.) And you say, خَفَتَ بِصَوْتِهِ , (Msb,) and بِهِ , (TA,) He lowered his voice; spoke with a low voice. (Msb, TA.) And خَفَتَ بِقِرَآءَتِهِ ; (TA;) and بِهَا , (A, Msb,) inf. n. مُخَافَتَةٌ ; (Msb;) and ; (TA;) He lowered his voice in his reading or reciting; read, or recited, with a low voice: (A, Msb, TA:) or the second of these signifies he read, or recited, indistinctly, not with raised voice. (Lth, TA.) -b5- خَفَتَ , said of seed-produce, (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, such as is termed خَافِتٌ [explained below]. (Msb.)

headwords.def: خَفَتَ خاف خف خفى خفت خفتت, (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. خَفِتَ, (Msb,) inf. n. خُفُوتٌ (S, A, K) and خَفْتٌ (Msb, TA) and خُفَاتٌ, (TA,) It (the voice, S, A, Msb) was, or became, still, (S, K,) or silent; (A;) was, or became, low, (Msb,) or soft, or gentle, or slender; and became weak, by reason of vehement hunger. (TA.) Hence, said of a dying man, He ceased speaking; (S;) he was, or became, silent; (S, A, K;) he spoke not. (A.) And [hence,] خَفَتَ, (A, TA,) inf. n. خُفُوتٌ.
خفّت خاف خف خفى خفت خفتت [app. It silenced, or killed: said of a smiting with a sword or the like: see فَوَّارٌ ]. (TA.)
خافت خاف خافت خافتت, inf. n. مُخَافَتَةٌ: see 1, in four places. [Hence,] الإِبِلُ تُخَافِتُ المَضْغَ The camels ruminate. (TA.)
اخفتت أخفت أخفتت اخفتت She (a camel) brought forth on the day [ of the year ] in which she was impregnated [or just a year after she was covered ]. (K.)
تخافتوا تخافتوا خافت They consulted together secretly. (TA.) See also 1. And تخافت (assumed tropical:) He feigned, or made a false show of, weakness and stillness. (TA.)

خَفْتٌ خاف خف خفى خفت خفتت (S) and, (A,) applied to speech, (S, A,) Uttered with a low, or suppressed, voice. (S, * A.) [See also خَافِتٌ.] The former is also syn. with خَبْتٌ [ A low, or depressed, tract of ground: &c.]. (K. [So accord. to my MS. copy of the K, and accord. to the TA: but in the CK this signification is omitted; for instead of والخَبْتُ وَبِالضَّمِّ السَّ َابُ, we find وَالخَفْتُ بِالفَتْحِ وَبِالضَّمِّ السَّ َابُ, meaning that حَفْتٌ and خُفْتٌ signify the same as سَ َابٌ.])
خُفْتٌ خاف خف خفى خفت خفتت [and accord. to the CK خَفْتٌ, but this is app. a mistake, (see what next precedes,)] i. q. سَ َابٌ [i. e. Rue ]; (K;) as also خُتْفٌ. (T, TA.)

خُفَاتٌ خفات [an inf. n. of 1, q. v. And also used as an epithet; for ُو خُفَاتٍ ]: see خَفْتٌ. Also Weak hearing. (TA, from a trad.) لَسْتُ خُفَاتًا [ I am not weak, and abject, or abased ]. (T, from a verse of El-Jaadee.)

خَفُوتٌ خفوت (tropical:) A lean, or an emaciated, woman: (Lh, K:) or a woman who is scarcely seen distinctly, by reason of leanness, or emaciation: (TA:) or a woman who is deemed goodly, or beautiful, (K,) whom the eye regards as worthy of notice, (A, TA,) as long as she is alone, not when she is among other women. (A, K, TA.) You say اِمْرَأَةٌ خَفْوتٌ لَفُوتٌ: (Lth, A, TA:) لفوت meaning wont to calumniate, or slander.
خَفِيتٌ خفى خفي خفيت: see what follows, in two places.

خَافِتٌ خاف خافت خافتت A voice becoming still, or silent; or low, or suppressed; as also. (A.) You say صَوْتٌ خَفِيضٌ. (TA.) One whose voice is still, or silent, by reason of his weakness. (Har p. 76.) Applied to a dying man, Ceasing to speak; silent. (S.) سَحَابٌ خَافِتٌ Clouds in which is no water.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
